questions.problem:
Suppose that $|\,m\,|=12$, $|\,n\,|=9$ and that the angle between the vectors is $\theta ={30}^{∘}.$ Find the vector projection of $m$ onto $n$ in terms of the vector $n.$

${\text{proj}}_{n}\,m=$
{{field-1}}
$n$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the scalar projection as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{n}\,m & =|\,m\,|\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =12\operatorname{cos}⁡({30}^{∘}) \\  & =12\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\  & =6\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the unit vector that is parallel to $n:$

$$
u=\frac{n}{|\,n\,|}=\frac{n}{9}=\frac{1}{9}n
$$

Finally, we compute the vector projection as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{n}\,m & ={\text{comp}}_{n}\,m\cdot u \\  & =6\sqrt{3}\cdot \frac{1}{9}n \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}n\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Suppose that $|\,c\,|=10$, $|\,d\,|=2\sqrt{3}$ and that the angle between the vectors is $\theta ={30}^{∘}.$ Find the vector projection of $c$ onto $d$ in terms of the vector $d.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the scalar projection as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{d}\,c & =|\,c\,|\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =10\operatorname{cos}⁡({30}^{∘}) \\  & =10\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\  & =5\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the unit vector that is parallel to $d:$

$$
u=\frac{d}{|\,d\,|}=\frac{d}{2\sqrt{3}}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{3}}d
$$

Finally, we compute the vector projection as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{d}\,c & ={\text{comp}}_{d}\,c\cdot u \\  & =5\sqrt{3}\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{3}}d \\  & =\frac{5}{2}d\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{b}\,a & =|\,a\,|\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =6\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}) \\  & =6\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Suppose that $|\,p\,|=4\sqrt{2}$, $|\,q\,|=16$ and that the angle between the vectors is $\theta ={45}^{∘}.$ Find the vector projection of $q$ onto $p$ in terms of the vector $p.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the scalar projection as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{p}\,q & =|\,q\,|\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =16\operatorname{cos}⁡({45}^{∘}) \\  & =16\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\  & =8\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the unit vector that is parallel to $p:$

$$
u=\frac{p}{|\,p\,|}=\frac{p}{4\sqrt{2}}=\frac{1}{4\sqrt{2}}p
$$

Finally, we compute the vector projection as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{p}\,q & ={\text{comp}}_{p}\,q\cdot u \\  & =8\sqrt{2}\cdot \frac{1}{4\sqrt{2}}p \\  & =2p\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Let $a=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 8 \\ 3\end{aligned}]$ and $b=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Find the vector projection of $a$ onto $b.$
questions.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the vector projection, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,a & =\frac{a\cdot b}{b\cdot b}b \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{a}_{z}{b}_{z}}{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}+{b}_{z}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{1\cdot 7+8\cdot (-2)+3\cdot 1}{{7}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{1}^{2}}b \\  & =-\frac{6}{54}⟨7,-2,1⟩ \\  & =-\frac{1}{9}⟨7,-2,1⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{7}{9},\frac{2}{9},-\frac{1}{9}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Let $a=⟨0,-3,1⟩$ and $b=⟨\sqrt{2},1,0⟩.$ Find the vector projection of $a$ onto $b.$
questions.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the vector projection, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,a & =\frac{a\cdot b}{b\cdot b}b \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{a}_{z}{b}_{z}}{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}+{b}_{z}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{0\cdot \sqrt{2}+(-3)\cdot 1+1\cdot 0}{(\sqrt{2})^{2}+{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{-3}{3}⟨\sqrt{2},1,0⟩ \\  & =⟨-\sqrt{2},-1,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Let $c=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$ and $d=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{aligned}].$ Find the vector projection of $d$ onto $c.$
questions.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the vector projection, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{c}\,d & =\frac{c\cdot d}{c\cdot c}c \\  & =\frac{{c}_{x}{d}_{x}+{c}_{y}{d}_{y}+{c}_{z}{d}_{z}}{{c}_{x}^{2}+{c}_{y}^{2}+{c}_{z}^{2}}c \\  & =\frac{2\cdot 2+1\cdot (-3)+(-3)\cdot 5}{{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-3)^{2}}c \\  & =-\frac{14}{14}⟨2,1,-3⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,-1,3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Since $a$ is a nonzero vector, its projection onto another nonzero vector $b$ equals the zero vector only when the vectors are perpendicular. 

So, we must have

$$
a⊥b\,⟹\,a\cdot b=0.
$$

Computing the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & ={a}_{x}\cdot {b}_{x}+{a}_{y}\cdot {b}_{y}+{a}_{z}\cdot {b}_{z} \\  & =-2\cdot x+1\cdot 3+2\cdot 1 \\  & =-2x+5.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & =0 \\ -2x+5 & =0 \\ 2x & =5 \\ x & =\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Let $a=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ and $b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ x\end{aligned}].$ Given that the projection of $a$ onto $b$ is the zero vector, find the value of $x.$
questions.worked_solution:
Since $a$ is a nonzero vector, its projection onto another nonzero vector $b$ equals the zero vector only when the vectors are perpendicular. 

So, we must have

$$
a⊥b\,⟹\,a\cdot b=0.
$$

Computing the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & ={a}_{x}\cdot {b}_{x}+{a}_{y}\cdot {b}_{y}+{a}_{z}\cdot {b}_{z} \\  & =1\cdot 1+3\cdot (-2)+2\cdot x \\  & =2x-5.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & =0 \\ 2x-5 & =0 \\ 2x & =5 \\ x & =\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Let $a=⟨1,-2,5⟩$ and $b=⟨3,-1,-1⟩.$ Find the vector projection of $a$ onto $b.$
questions.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the vector projection, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,a & =\frac{a\cdot b}{b\cdot b}b \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{a}_{z}{b}_{z}}{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}+{b}_{z}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{1\cdot 3+(-2)\cdot (-1)+5\cdot (-1)}{{3}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{0}{{3}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}}b \\  & =⟨0,0,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Let $a=⟨1,2,3⟩$ and $b=⟨2,-3,x⟩.$ Given that the projection of $a$ onto $b$ is the zero vector, find the value of $x.$
questions.worked_solution:
Since $a$ is a nonzero vector, its projection onto another nonzero vector $b$ equals the zero vector only when the vectors are perpendicular. 

So, we must have

$$
a⊥b\,⟹\,a\cdot b=0.
$$

Computing the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & ={a}_{x}\cdot {b}_{x}+{a}_{y}\cdot {b}_{y}+{a}_{z}\cdot {b}_{z} \\  & =1\cdot 2+2\cdot (-3)+3\cdot x \\  & =3x-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & =0 \\ 3x-4 & =0 \\ 3x & =4 \\ x & =\frac{4}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Let $a=⟨-2,3,1⟩$ and $b=⟨-1,-2,x⟩.$ Given that the projection of $a$ onto $b$ is the zero vector, find the value of $x.$
questions.worked_solution:
Since $a$ is a nonzero vector, its projection onto another nonzero vector $b$ equals the zero vector only when the vectors are perpendicular. 

So, we must have

$$
a⊥b\,⟹\,a\cdot b=0.
$$

Computing the dot product, we obtain

$$

$$

$$

canonical_examples.problem: Suppose that $|\,\mathbf{a}\,|=8,|\,\mathbf{b}\,|=4$ and that the angle between the vectors is $\theta = \dfrac{5\pi}{6}.$ Find the vector projection of $\mathbf{a}$ onto $\mathbf{b}$ in terms of the vector $\mathbf{b}.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we find the scalar projection as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{b}\,a & =|\,a\,|\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =8\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{6}) \\  & =8\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) \\  & =-4\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the unit vector that is parallel to $\mathbf{b}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\mathbf{u} = \dfrac{\mathbf{b}}{|\,\mathbf{b}\,|} = \dfrac{\mathbf{b}}{4} = \dfrac{1}{4} \mathbf{b}
$$

Finally, we compute the vector projection as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,a & ={\text{comp}}_{b}\,a\cdot u \\  & =-4\sqrt{3}\cdot \frac{1}{4}b \\  & =-\sqrt{3}b\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Let $\mathbf{a}=\langle 1,-3,5 \rangle$ and $\mathbf{b}=\langle 5,-4,0 \rangle$. Find the vector projection of $\mathbf{a}$ onto $\mathbf{b}$.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the vector projection, we obtain

$$

$$
